references.text: After the flood, God gives Noah permission to eat meat but forbids eating meat with its blood in it, establishing the fundamental prohibition against consuming blood.
A perpetual statute that forbids the Israelites from eating fat and blood, confirming the blood prohibition as a lasting law.
An expanded explanation of the prohibition against eating blood, with the reasoning that blood is the seat of life and must be used for atonement on the altar.
Reiterates the prohibition against eating anything containing blood, as part of the holiness code.
Moses repeats the prohibition against eating blood; the blood must be poured out on the ground like water.
Elaborates on the prohibition against eating blood with the reasoning that blood is life, and that it will go well with those who obey this commandment.
Prohibition against eating blood; it must be poured out on the ground like water, in connection with rules concerning the firstfruits.
Saul prevents the people from sinning by eating meat with its blood in it and ensures that animals are slaughtered properly.
Ezekiel rebukes those who eat meat with its blood in it as a sign of their uncleanness.
The Jerusalem council requires Gentile Christians to abstain from blood, continuing the blood prohibition into the new covenant.
The apostolic letter confirms that believers must keep away from blood as part of the necessary things.
Paul reminds them of the decision made at the Jerusalem council, including the prohibition against blood, which applies to Gentile Christians.
